applies_why: Yes: it weighs the challenger's and defender's chains by explicit naming/inference rather than by footing alone.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'by footing' — whether a footed chain may be deemed underdetermined because it does not explicitly name Joseph (stating-verse reading) or whether support alone governs and explicit naming is irrelevant (chain-footing reading).
why: The judge treats footed chains as underdetermined because one does not explicitly name Joseph and the other relies on an inference, which is a verse-by-verse stating requirement and not a chain-against-chain footing comparison.
